correctness.rationale: The step-killing Feynman–Kac Neumann problem is explicitly solved and its unique bounded matching solution gives the complete interarrival Laplace transform. Expansion at s=0 yields exact E T and Var T; iid postreset regeneration and a finite-variance nonlattice renewal counting limit give the Fano function. Exact algebra proves a single crossing at a=sqrt(3/2) and a unique minimum because 2a³+6a²+3a-3 is strictly increasing for a>0. CHECK.py independently verifies rational identities and a finite-difference killed-generator solution with 130 tests; finite discretizations are cross-checks only.

originality.rationale: Plata–Gupta–Azaele 2020 fully treats the exact spatial threshold resetting model but studies stationary density and absorption-first-passage time rather than the fluctuations of effective reset counts. Roldán–Gupta 2017 supplies a general first-reset distribution framework for arbitrary spatial hazards, making the Laplace-transform method an anticipated specialization; the evaluated reflected-step transform and its sharp full counting-noise phase diagram are not established in the worked examples inspected. General renewal asymptotics of Godrèche–Luck 2023 alone do not determine the interarrival moments. Semantically related published threshold-triggered diffusion results reset on boundary hitting, with a different clock. No exact earlier Fano crossing or minimizer was located; implicit mathematical subsumption and unknown priority are explicitly retained as risk.
residual_risks: Generic first-reset resolvent methods of Roldán–Gupta (2017) could implicitly subsume the transform; a specialized earlier computation might derive the same Fano threshold without matching the title or wording.
Indexed public research results with only title/summary material were compared on their stated claims; their unpublished-to-this-review details cannot be excluded.
Independent human publication-priority validation has not been performed.

value.rationale: Effective reset-event count measures catastrophe frequency and temporal regularity directly in a studied asymmetric stochastic resetting mechanism. The sharp weak-intensity sub-Poisson/high-intensity super-Poisson transition and unique optimal precision reveal a competition not recoverable from the published stationary one-point law alone. The full quantitative threshold and global minimizer are natural, exact and informative for counting noise, not a tiny arbitrary slice. The domain is restricted to an ideal half-line step-hazard diffusion and long-time counts.
